mainTopic: Rain as birth and blessing, prayer in times of trouble, hidden ברכה, and רבי יוחנן's teachings on rain
overview: This amud is a collection of teachings about rain and prayer. First, ריש לקיש shows three words that the תנ"ך uses both for a woman having children and for rain: עצירה, לידה, and פקידה. A ברייתא then explains that the 'פלג אלהים' is a vault in the sky that the rain comes out of. רבי שמואל בר נחמני explains a פסוק in איוב about rain that comes as punishment or as kindness. The amud then tells two stories about prayer in hard times: praying about a famine rather than a plague, and רבי זירא accepting a fast during a decree that banned fasting. Next, רבי יצחק and others teach that rain at the wrong time is a hardship, while rain in its proper time brings ברכה. They also teach that ברכה rests only on things hidden from the eye, and a ברייתא applies this to a farmer measuring his grain. Finally, the גמרא gives a סימן for five teachings of רבי יוחנן about rain. It teaches three of them here and begins the fourth, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: First parallel: closing up a womb and closing up the sky
steps.stepSummary: The same word, עצירה (closing up), is used for a woman who cannot have children and for the sky when it holds back rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'closing up' is used about a woman, as it says: 'For ה׳ had closed up every womb.' And 'closing up' is used about rain, as it is written: 'And He will close up the heavens.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש begins his list of words that link a woman and rain. The first word is עצירה, 'closing up.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: In בראשית‎, ה׳ 'closed up' the wombs in אבימלך's house so no one could give birth. In דברים‎, ה׳ warns that He will 'close up' the sky so no rain falls. Because the תורה uses the same word for both, rain is pictured like a birth that can be held back or allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: 'Closing up' is stated regarding a woman,
as it is said: 'For ה׳ had closed up,
phrases.notes: בראשית כ:יח, about the household of אבימלך

phrases.english: every womb,'
and 'closing up' is stated regarding rains,
as it is written: 'And He will close up the heavens.'
phrases.notes: דברים יא:יז, from the second paragraph of קריאת שמע

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues ריש לקיש's comparison of rain to childbirth from the previous section of the דף.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word עצירה links a woman's inability to give birth with the sky holding back rain.

steps.title: Second parallel: a woman gives birth and rain makes the earth give birth
steps.stepSummary: The word לידה (giving birth) is used for a woman and also for what rain does to the earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Giving birth' is used about a woman, and 'giving birth' is used about rain. About a woman, it is written: 'And she conceived and gave birth to a son.' About rain, it is written: 'And it makes it give birth and sprout.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש brings his second word that links a woman and rain: לידה, 'giving birth.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a woman is about רחל finally having a son. The פסוק about rain is from ישעיה: the rain waters the ground and 'makes it give birth' to plants. So rain does not only come down. It makes the earth produce new life, just like a birth.

keyTerms.meaning: And it made it give birth

phrases.english: 'Giving birth' is stated regarding a woman
and 'giving birth' is stated regarding rains.
'Giving birth' is stated regarding a woman,
as it is written: 'And she conceived and gave birth to a son,'
phrases.notes: בראשית ל:כג, about רחל

phrases.english: and 'giving birth' is stated regarding rains,
as it is written: 'And it makes it give birth and sprout.'
phrases.notes: ישעיה נה:י, where the rain waters the earth

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֱמַר לֵידָה בְּאִשָּׁה וְנֶאֱמַר לֵידָה בִּגְשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second shared word to the list started in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word לידה links a woman giving birth with rain causing the earth to produce.

steps.title: Third parallel: ה׳ remembers a woman and remembers the land
steps.stepSummary: The word פקידה (remembering) is used when ה׳ remembered שרה and when He 'remembered' the land with rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Remembering' is used about a woman, and 'remembering' is used about rain. About a woman, it is written: 'And ה׳ remembered שרה.' About rain, it is written: 'You remembered the land and watered it, You greatly enrich it, with the channel of God full of water.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש finishes his list with the third word: פקידה, 'remembering.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ 'remembered' שרה, and she had יצחק. In תהלים‎, ה׳ 'remembered' the land by watering it. In both cases, ה׳'s attention brings new life after a time of waiting. The rain פסוק ends with the phrase פלג אלהים מלא מים, which the גמרא explains next.
steps.whatToRemember: ריש לקיש lists three words, עצירה, לידה, and פקידה. Each one is used both for a woman having children and for rain. The lesson: rain is like a birth. ה׳ holds it back or remembers and brings it.

phrases.english: 'Remembering' is stated regarding a woman,
and 'remembering' is stated regarding rains.
'Remembering' is stated regarding a woman,
as it is written: 'And ה׳ remembered Sarah,'
phrases.notes: בראשית כא:א

phrases.english: and 'remembering' is stated regarding rains,
as it is written: 'You remembered the land and watered it,
phrases.notes: תהלים סה:י

phrases.english: You greatly enrich it,
the channel of God is full of water.'

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֱמַר פְּקִידָה בְּאִשָּׁה, וְנֶאֱמַר פְּקִידָה בִּגְשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the third and final shared word, completing ריש לקיש's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word פקידה links ה׳ remembering a barren woman with ה׳ watering the land.

steps.title: What does the channel of God full of water mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא stops to ask about a phrase in the last פסוק: what is the 'channel of God that is full of water'?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'the channel of God full of water'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns aside to explain an unclear phrase from the פסוק it just quoted. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on ריש לקיש. It is a simple question about what the words mean. The phrase sounds like there is a real 'channel' of water belonging to ה׳, and the גמרא wants to know what that is.

phrases.english: What is 'the channel of God full of water'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up a phrase from the פסוק quoted at the end of step 3 and asks what it means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the phrase פלג אלהים מלא מים in תהלים סה:י.

steps.title: A vault in the sky that the rain comes out of
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that there is a kind of vault (קובה) in the sky, and the rain comes out of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: There is something like a vault in the sky, and the rain comes out of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question by quoting a ברייתא. The 'channel of God' is a vault-like storehouse in the sky that rain comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תנא tells us the answer comes from a ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים. The 'channel of God full of water' is read as a real holding place in the רקיע. Rain is let out from it, which fits the idea that ה׳ opens and closes the rain.

phrases.english: It was taught: There is a kind of vault in the sky,
from which the rains come out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: פלג אלהים is a vault (קובה) in the רקיע from which the rain comes out.

steps.title: Rain for punishment or for kindness
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני explains a פסוק in איוב: rain can fall where it is wasted or where it helps.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: What does the פסוק mean, 'Whether for a rod, or for His land, or for kindness, He brings it'? 'For a rod' (punishment) means the rain falls on mountains and hills. 'For kindness He brings it to His land' means it falls on fields and vineyards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps discussing rain and brings a new explanation of a פסוק in איוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same rain can be a punishment or a blessing. It depends on where it lands. When the people are judged badly, the rain falls on mountains and hills, where it does little good. When they are judged well, it falls on fields and vineyards, where crops grow.

keyTerms.meaning: A rod, which means punishment or correction
He causes it (the rain) to come
Mountains and hills, places where rain is mostly wasted
Fields and vineyards, places where rain helps

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said,
What is the meaning of what is written:
"Whether for a rod, or for His land,
phrases.notes: From איוב 37:13

phrases.english: or for kindness, He causes it to come."
"Whether for a rod" means on mountains and hills,
phrases.notes: Punishment: the rain lands where it is wasted

phrases.english: "For kindness He brings it to His land" means
phrases.notes: He reads 'His land' together with 'kindness'

phrases.english: on fields and on vineyards.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי, מַאי דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching about rain from a different חכם, רבי שמואל בר נחמני, continuing the theme of rain from the earlier steps.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain as punishment falls on mountains and hills. Rain as kindness falls on fields and vineyards.

steps.title: A second reading: trees, seeds, and stored water
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק is explained another way, with three levels of benefit from rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Whether for a rod' means the rain helps only the trees. 'Or for His land' means it helps only the seeds. 'Or for kindness He brings it' means it fills the cisterns, ditches, and caves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second explanation of the same פסוק, splitting it into three parts instead of two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here each phrase is a different level of blessing. The lowest level helps only trees. The next level helps seeds. The highest level, 'kindness,' is so much rain that it fills water storage for the dry season.
steps.confusionAlert: In the first reading, 'rod' meant the rain was wasted. In this reading, even the 'rod' level still helps trees a little. Each phrase is now one level higher than the one before it.

phrases.english: "Whether for a rod" means for the trees,
"Or for His land" means for the seeds,
"Or for kindness He causes it to come" means
cisterns, ditches, and caves are filled.
phrases.notes: Enough water to last through the dry season

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second way to read the same פסוק from step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rod means rain for trees, His land means rain for seeds, and kindness means rain that fills water storage.

steps.title: Famine and plague: which one do we pray for?
steps.stepSummary: In רבי שמואל בר נחמני's time there was both a famine and a plague, and the חכמים had to decide what to pray for.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the days of רבי שמואל בר נחמני there was a famine and a plague. They said: What should we do? Pray for both? That is not possible. So let us pray about the plague, and we will put up with the famine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about two troubles at once. The חכמים assume they may pray for only one, and they lean toward praying about the plague. This sets up רבי שמואל בר נחמני's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים take it as a given that you cannot pray about two troubles together. Their first idea is to pray about the plague and to put up with the famine.

keyTerms.meaning: We will bear it, put up with it

phrases.english: In the days of Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani
there was a famine and a plague.
They said: What should we do?
Should we pray for mercy for both? That is not possible.
phrases.notes: We do not pray about two troubles at once

phrases.english: Rather, let us pray for mercy about the plague,
and the famine we will bear.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּימֵי רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי הֲוָה כַּפְנָא וּמוֹתָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story told about the same חכם
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which trouble should we pray about, when we may pray about only one?

steps.title: Pray for food, since food is given to the living
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני says to pray about the famine, because when ה׳ gives plenty, He gives it to living people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said to them: Let us pray about the famine. When ה׳ gives plenty, He gives it to the living, as it says: 'You open Your hand and satisfy every living thing with favor.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמואל בר נחמני disagrees with the חכמים and tells them to pray about the famine instead of the plague.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His logic is that food is given to 'every living thing,' so if ה׳ ends the famine, people must be alive to eat. That means the plague will stop too. One prayer ends up solving both troubles without praying for two.
steps.whatToRemember: When two troubles come together, pray about the famine. ה׳ gives food to living people, so the plague will end as well.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said to them:
Let us pray for mercy about the famine,
because when the Merciful One gives plenty,
it is to the living that He gives it,
phrases.notes: So the plague must end too

phrases.english: as it is written: "You open Your hand
and satisfy every living thing with favor."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי נִיבְעֵי רַחֲמֵי אַכַּפְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the חכמים' question and rejects their plan to pray about the plague
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Pray about the famine, because food is given only to the living, so the plague will end as well.

steps.title: Where do we learn not to pray for two troubles?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the rule the חכמים assumed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that we do not pray for two things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask where the rule in the story comes from. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the story, everyone took it for granted that you cannot pray about two troubles at once. Now the גמרא wants a פסוק that teaches this rule.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that we do not pray for two things?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule the חכמים assumed in step 8
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק that teaches we do not pray about two troubles at once

steps.title: Proof from עזרא: 'for this'
steps.stepSummary: The words 'for this' in עזרא show that they prayed about one trouble even though there was another one.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'So we fasted and asked our God for this.' This shows that there was another trouble.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק from עזרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says they prayed 'for this,' meaning one specific thing. Saying 'this' suggests there was another trouble they did not pray about. So they chose to pray about only one.

keyTerms.meaning: For this, about this one thing

phrases.english: As it is written: "So we fasted and asked
of our God for this."
phrases.notes: עזרא 8:23

phrases.english: This implies that there was another trouble.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב וַנָּצוּמָה וַנְּבַקְשָׁה מֵאֱלֹהֵינוּ עַל זֹאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: עזרא prayed 'for this,' which implies another trouble they did not pray about.

steps.title: A second proof from דניאל, said in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: In ארץ ישראל they learned the same rule from a פסוק in דניאל, in the name of רבי חגי.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West (ארץ ישראל) they say in the name of רבי חגי that we learn it from here: 'To ask mercy from the God of Heaven about this secret.' This shows that there was another trouble.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different פסוק for the same rule, as taught in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works the same way as before: 'this secret' points to one specific request. That implies there was another trouble they did not ask about. Only the פסוק has changed, from עזרא to דניאל.
steps.whatToRemember: We do not pray about two troubles at once. We learn it from 'for this' in עזרא, or in ארץ ישראל from 'this secret' in דניאל.

phrases.english: In the West they say
in the name of Rabbi Chaggai: it is from here:
"And to ask mercy from before
the God of Heaven about this secret."
phrases.notes: דניאל 2:18

phrases.english: This implies that there was another trouble.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַעְרְבָא אָמְרִי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חַגַּי מֵהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another source for the same rule proven in step 11
steps.raayaObject: The rule that we do not pray about two troubles at once

steps.title: Accepting a fast during a decree against fasting
steps.stepSummary: During a שמד that banned fasting, רבי זירא told the people to accept a fast now and keep it once the decree ended.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the days of רבי זירא, the government made a decree of persecution, and it also forbade fasting. רבי זירא said: Let us accept the fast on ourselves now, and when the decree goes away, we will actually fast.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. Jews could not fast to pray against the decree, because fasting itself was banned. רבי זירא found a solution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally you fast to pray about a trouble. Here the trouble itself blocked the fast. רבי זירא says the act of accepting the fast already has value, even if the actual fasting comes later.

keyTerms.meaning: To sit in a fast, meaning to observe a fast
Let us accept it on ourselves

steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא is not saying to skip the fast. The people take on the fast now and really fast later, after the decree ends.

phrases.english: In the days of Rabbi Zeira they decreed a religious persecution,
and they decreed that people may not observe a fast.
Rabbi Zeira said to them:
Let us accept it (the fast) upon ourselves,
and when the persecution ends, we will observe it.
phrases.notes: The fast is accepted now and kept later.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second story like the one about רבי שמואל בר נחמני: what to do about fasting and prayer when there is a hard situation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When you cannot fast because of a decree, you may accept the fast now and keep it once the decree ends.

steps.title: The people ask for the source
steps.stepSummary: The people ask רבי זירא how he knows that accepting a fast you cannot yet keep is worth anything.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: From where do you know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The people ask רבי זירא for his source. This sets up the proof he brings in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is not obvious that only accepting a fast, without fasting, does anything. So they want a פסוק that shows the acceptance itself counts.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this?

phrases.english: They said to him: From where do you have this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי זירא's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that accepting a fast already has value before you actually fast.

steps.title: Proof from דניאל: prayers were heard from the first day
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא quotes the מלאך telling דניאל that his words were heard from the first day he set his heart to fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: As it is written: 'He said to me: Do not be afraid, דניאל, because from the first day that you set your heart to understand and to fast before your God, your words were heard.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers with a פסוק. דניאל was answered from the moment he decided to fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'from the first day you set your heart.' That means the decision to fast is what made the prayer heard, not only the fasting itself. So accepting a fast now already works, even if you fast later.

keyTerms.meaning: You set your heart, meaning you decided

steps.whatToRemember: Accepting a fast with your heart already makes your prayer heard. That is why you may accept a fast now and keep it later.

phrases.english: He said to them: As it is written:
'And he said to me: Do not fear, Daniel,
for from the first day
that you set your heart to understand
and to fast before your God,
your words were heard.'
phrases.notes: Key point: the prayer was heard from the moment of the decision.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in דניאל shows that prayer is heard from the moment a person decides to fast.

steps.title: Rain on ערב שבת is a sign of a curse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says that even in a terrible drought, rain on ערב שבת is a sign of a curse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Even in years like the years of אליהו, when there was no rain, if rain falls on Fridays, it is only a sign of a curse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the topic of rain. רבי יצחק says rain at the wrong time, on ערב שבת, is bad even when rain is badly needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the days of אליהו there was a terrible drought, so any rain should feel like a ברכה. Still, rain on ערב שבת gets in the way of people preparing for שבת, so it counts as a curse.

keyTerms.meaning: The years of אליהו, a time of severe drought

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Even in years like the years of Elijah,
if rain falls on Shabbat eves,
it is nothing but a sign of a curse.
phrases.notes: It disturbs the preparations for Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: אֲפִילּוּ שָׁנִים כִּשְׁנֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from fasting and goes back to the topic of rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain on ערב שבת is a sign of a curse, even during a drought.

steps.title: A rainy day is as hard as a day of judgment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא links רבי יצחק's teaching to רבה בר שילא, who says a rainy day is as hard as a day of judgment.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבה בר שילא said: A day of rain is as hard as a day of judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that another אמורא said the same kind of idea. Rain can make life hard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'היינו דאמר' mean 'this matches what someone else said.' רבה בר שילא's line supports רבי יצחק's point that rain is not always pleasant.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the same as what was said

phrases.english: This is what Rabba bar Sheila said:
A rainy day is as difficult as a day of judgment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 16 with a matching statement.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that rain can be a hardship

steps.title: אמימר: we would pray against rain if it were not needed
steps.stepSummary: אמימר says that if the world did not need rain, we would pray for it to stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: If it were not that people need it, we would pray for mercy and cancel rain.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר takes the idea even further. Rain is such a bother that the only reason we do not pray against it is that people need it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds to the last two steps. Rain has a real cost in daily life. We accept it only because the world cannot live without it.

keyTerms.meaning: We would ask for mercy, meaning we would pray

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
If not for the fact that it is needed by people,
we would pray for mercy and cancel it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַמֵּימָר: אִי לָא דִּצְרִיךְ לִבְרִיָּיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes the idea of rain as a hardship even further.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain is a hardship. We accept it only because the world needs it.

steps.title: Sun on שבת is charity for the poor
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says that sun on שבת is צדקה for the poor, and he brings a פסוק from מלאכי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק also said: Sun on שבת is charity for the poor, as it says: 'For you who fear My name, the sun of charity and healing will shine.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is another teaching from רבי יצחק. It is the opposite of rain on ערב שבת: sun on שבת is a gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Poor people have little to keep them warm. Sun on שבת lets them enjoy the day. The פסוק calls the sun 'שמש צדקה,' sun of charity.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said, introducing a פסוק

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Sun on Shabbat is charity for the poor,
as it is said: 'And there shall shine for you who fear My name
a sun of charity and healing.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching from רבי יצחק, the opposite side of his rain teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sun on שבת is a kindness for the poor.

steps.title: A day of rain brings blessing even to a coin
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק says that a day of rain is great, because even a פרוטה in the pocket is blessed, as the פסוק in דברים shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: Great is the day of rain, because even a פרוטה in the pocket is blessed on it, as it says: 'To give the rain of your land in its time, and to bless all the work of your hands.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק praises rain that comes at the right time. It brings ברכה to everything, even money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the focus was on rain at a bad time. Here the point is that rain in its proper time is a huge ברכה. The פסוק joins rain with 'blessing all the work of your hands,' so the ברכה reaches beyond the crops.

keyTerms.meaning: Great is the day of rain
A small coin in the pocket

steps.whatToRemember: Rain at the wrong time, like ערב שבת, is a hardship. Rain in its proper time is a great ברכה that reaches everything, even a coin in your pocket.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Great is the day of rains,
for even a peruta in the pocket is blessed on it,
as it is said: 'To give the rain of your land in its time
and to bless all the work of your hand.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: גָּדוֹל יוֹם הַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching from רבי יצחק, praising rain that comes in its proper time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain in its time brings ברכה to everything, even money.

steps.title: Blessing is found only in what is hidden from the eye
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that ברכה rests only on things hidden from view, based on a פסוק about barns (אסמיך).
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said: Blessing is found only in something hidden from the eye, as it says: 'ה׳ will command the blessing for you in your barns.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק gives a new teaching. ברכה only rests on things that are hidden and not openly looked at.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is a wordplay. בַּאֲסָמֶיךָ (your barns) sounds like סָמוּי (hidden), so the barn stands for stored produce that nobody is watching. This follows step 20, which said that even a פרוטה in the pocket is blessed on a rainy day.

keyTerms.meaning: Blessing, meaning extra abundance from ה׳
Hidden from the eye, not openly seen
Your barns or storehouses (sounds like סָמוּי)

steps.whyThisMatters: This idea is the base for the practical ברייתא about measuring grain in the next steps.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Blessing is not found
except in something hidden from the eye,
as it is stated: 'The Lord will command for you
phrases.notes: דברים כח:ח

phrases.english: the blessing in your barns.'
phrases.notes: אסמיך is read as related to סמוי, meaning hidden

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי יצחק's teachings about blessing, following the idea of the blessed פרוטה in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברכה rests only on things hidden from the eye, learned from אסמיך.

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל teaches the same idea
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from דבי רבי ישמעאל says the same thing: ברכה rests only where the eye has no control, using the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: Blessing is found only in something the eye does not control, as it says: 'ה׳ will command the blessing for you in your barns.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רבי יצחק's teaching with almost the same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording is slightly different. Instead of 'hidden from the eye' it says 'the eye does not control it', but the meaning and the פסוק are the same. This shows that רבי יצחק's idea is also an older ברייתא tradition.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא taught in the study hall of רבי ישמעאל

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Blessing is not found

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּדָבָר שֶׁאֵין הָעַיִן שׁוֹלֶטֶת בּוֹ,
phrases.english: except in something the eye does not control,
as it is stated: 'The Lord will command for you
the blessing in your barns.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 21 with a parallel ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יצחק's teaching that ברכה rests only on hidden things
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of דבי רבי ישמעאל, using the same פסוק

steps.title: The prayers a farmer says when measuring his grain
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says what a farmer says before he starts measuring his grain and what he says once he has begun.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Someone who goes in to measure his grain on the threshing floor says: 'May it be Your will, ה׳ our God, that You send blessing on the work of our hands.' Once he has started measuring, he says: 'Blessed is He Who sends blessing on this pile.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that turns the 'hidden blessing' idea into practice: what a farmer should pray when he measures his grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The farmer prays before he measures, while the amount is still unknown and ברכה can still come. Even after he begins measuring, he may still say a ברכה on the pile, because the full amount is not yet known.

keyTerms.meaning: His threshing floor, where grain is piled
May it be Your will (an opening for a prayer)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who goes in to measure his threshing floor says:
'May it be Your will, Lord our God,
that You send blessing on the work of our hands.'
Once he has begun to measure, he says:
'Blessed is He Who sends blessing on this pile.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the principle from steps 21 and 22 to a practical case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before measuring, the farmer says a יהי רצון for ברכה. Once he has started measuring, he says ברוך השולח ברכה בכרי הזה.

steps.title: Praying after measuring is a wasted prayer
steps.stepSummary: If the farmer measures first and only then prays, his prayer is a תפלת שוא, because ברכה does not rest on things that are weighed, measured, or counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he measured and only afterward prayed, this is a wasted prayer. This is because blessing is not found in something weighed, or measured, or counted, but only in something hidden from the eye.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes by teaching what is wrong to do: praying for ברכה after the amount is already known.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once grain is weighed, measured, or counted, the amount is fixed. Adding to it would be an open miracle, which ה׳ does not normally do. So the ברייתא ends by repeating the main rule: ברכה is found only in what is hidden from the eye.

keyTerms.meaning: A wasted prayer, a prayer said for nothing

steps.whatToRemember: ברכה works on what is still unknown and unseen. Once you have weighed, measured, or counted something, it is too late to pray for it to grow.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא shows in practice that a prayer for ברכה has to come while the amount is still unknown. Once the amount is fixed, the prayer is a תפלת שוא.

phrases.english: If he measured and afterward prayed for blessing,
this is a wasted prayer,
because blessing is not found
not in something weighed,
and not in something measured,
and not in something counted,
but only in something hidden from the eye.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא from step 23 with the wrong way to pray and the reason for it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Praying for ברכה after measuring is a תפלת שוא, since ברכה does not rest on weighed, measured, or counted things.

steps.title: A memory aid for five teachings of רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a סימן listing five key words, one for each of the five teachings of רבי יוחנן that follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Memory aid: Ingathering, armies, charity, tithe, provider.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא gives a list of key words to help us remember the five teachings of רבי יוחנן that are coming next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word points to one teaching: קיבוץ (ingathering of exiles), גייסות (armies), צדקה (charity), מעשר (tithe), and פרנס (community leader). Steps 26–29 teach the first three. Step 30 opens the fourth (מעשר), and the fourth and fifth teachings continue on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory aid that lists key words of upcoming teachings

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a teaching by itself. It is only a list of headings for the teachings that follow.

phrases.english: Ingathering, armies, charity,
tithe, provider: a memory aid.

steps.triggerLanguage: קִבּוּץ, גְּיָיסוֹת, צְדָקָה, מַעֲשֵׂר, פַּרְנָס סִימָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new group of teachings from רבי יוחנן about rain.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Lists the five teachings of רבי יוחנן that come next.

steps.title: A day of rain is as great as the ingathering of the exiles
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says a day of rain is as great as the day of קיבוץ גליות, based on a פסוק in תהלים that compares our return to אפיקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: A day of rain is as great as the day of the ingathering of the exiles, as it says: 'Return our captives, ה׳, like streams in the dry south.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the first teaching from the סימן (קיבוץ). He compares a rainy day to the day the Jewish people will be gathered back from exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares bringing back the exiles to אפיקים in the dry south (נגב). If אפיקים means rain, then the פסוק puts rain and קיבוץ גליות side by side. The next step proves that אפיקים does mean rain.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Great is the day of rain,
like the day of the ingathering of the exiles,
as it is stated: 'Return, O Lord, our captives
phrases.notes: תהלים קכו:ד

phrases.english: like streams in the dry south,'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: גָּדוֹל יוֹם הַגְּשָׁמִים כְּיוֹם קִבּוּץ גָּלִיּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first teaching listed in the סימן from step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A day of rain is as great as the day of קיבוץ גליות.

steps.title: Proof that the word for streams means rain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that אפיקים means rain, from a פסוק in שמואל ב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And 'streams' means nothing other than rain, as it says: 'And the streams of the sea appeared.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבי יוחנן's reading by showing that the word אפיקים refers to rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this proof, someone could say that אפיקים in the תהלים פסוק just means rivers, and then there would be no link to rain. A second פסוק shows that אפיקים is used for water that comes from rain, so the comparison to קיבוץ גליות holds.

phrases.english: and 'streams' means nothing but rain,
as it is stated: 'And the streams of the sea appeared.'
phrases.notes: שמואל ב כב:טז

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the word meaning that step 26 depends on.
steps.raayaObject: That אפיקים in תהלים קכו means rain

steps.title: On a day of rain even armies stop fighting
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says a day of rain is great because even armies stop on it, reading גדודיה in a פסוק in תהלים as 'its troops'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: A day of rain is great, because even armies stop on it, as it says: 'Watering its ridges, settling its furrows (troops).'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the second teaching from the סימן (גייסות). Rain is so great that even wars stop because of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, גְּדוּדֶיהָ means furrows, but the same word also means troops (גדוד). So 'settling its גדודים' hints that rain makes armies settle in place, because the mud stops them from fighting.

keyTerms.meaning: Its ridges or furrows in a field
Its furrows, which also suggests its troops

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Great is the day of rain,
for even armies stop on it,
as it is stated: 'Watering its ridges,'
phrases.notes: תהלים סה:יא

phrases.english: settling its furrows (troops).'
phrases.notes: גדודיה is read as troops

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: גָּדוֹל יוֹם הַגְּשָׁמִים שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ גְּיָיסוֹת פּוֹסְקוֹת בּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second teaching from the סימן in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain is so great that even armies stop fighting on a rainy day.

steps.title: Rain is held back because of false charity pledges
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says rain is withheld only because of people who pledge צדקה in public and do not give it, based on a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: Rain is held back only because of those who pledge charity in public and do not give, as it says: 'Clouds and wind but no rain: a man who boasts of a false gift.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the third teaching from the סימן (צדקה). רבי יוחנן explains that breaking public promises to give צדקה is the cause of drought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares clouds and wind that bring no rain to a man who boasts about a gift he never gives. רבי יוחנן reads this as cause and effect: the false public promise brings 'clouds without rain,' measure for measure. The empty promise produces an empty sky.

keyTerms.meaning: A false gift, a promised gift never given

steps.confusionAlert: Here פוסקי means 'those who pledge' (they fix an amount). In step 28, פוסקות meant 'stop'. It is the same root with a different meaning.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
Rains are not held back
except because of those who pledge charity in public
and do not give,
as it is stated: 'Clouds and wind,
phrases.notes: משלי כה:יד

phrases.english: and no rain:
a man who boasts of a false gift.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אֵין הַגְּשָׁמִים נֶעֱצָרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third teaching from the סימן in step 25.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a drought can come from failing to keep public promises of צדקה, which ties into the larger theme of מסכת תענית: finding the causes of drought and fixing them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain is withheld because of people who publicly pledge צדקה and do not give it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן introduces another verse to explain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces another teaching of רבי יוחנן with the opening formula 'מאי דכתיב,' preparing to quote and explain a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: What is the meaning of that which is written:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next teaching of רבי יוחנן, the fourth item in the סימן (מעשר). It announces that he will explain a פסוק, and that פסוק and its explanation come at the start of the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וְאָמַר' ('and he said') tells us this is another statement from the same רבי יוחנן, continuing the series of teachings flagged in the סימן. The phrase 'מַאי דִּכְתִיב' means 'what does this פסוק mean?' It does not attack anything. It is a standard way to introduce a new explanation of a verse.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he said.' It links this statement to the earlier teachings of the same speaker.
'What is the meaning of that which is written?' This is a formula that introduces a פסוק and its explanation.
A leading אמורא of ארץ ישראל. He is the author of the whole series of teachings here.

steps.confusionAlert: 'מַאי דִּכְתִיב' looks like a question, but nobody is being challenged. It is just an opening line. The answer is רבי יוחנן's own explanation of the פסוק that follows.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
phrases.notes: The 'and' shows this continues the series of רבי יוחנן's teachings.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of that which is written:
phrases.notes: An introductory formula. The פסוק being explained comes next in the text.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי יוחנן's teaching about people who pledge צדקה in public and do not give it (step 29), the גמרא moves to the next teaching in the series listed by the סימן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no ruling yet. This line only introduces רבי יוחנן's explanation of a פסוק that follows.
